text:
When I buy a mirror for the bathroom

I’ll look at my face

I’ll look at myself

for what other way is there, tell me

what other way to know who I am.

Whenever I lift my head

from the jumble of books and pages

and carry it, hollow and stuffed full

and let it rest there for a moment

I’ll look it in the eyes with a little

anxiety, curiosity, fear

or only with weariness, with boredom

with the old familiarity that belongs

or look at myself attentively, seriously

as that strange time—when I was eleven—

and say to myself, look, there you are

surely

I’ll think I don’t like it, or I’ll think

that face was the only one possible

and I’ll tell myself that’s me, that’s Idea

and smile at myself, giving myself courage.

translation.title: When I Buy a Mirror for the Bathroom
